title: People
markdown:
**What it is:** Everyone the Executive knows about, in two tabs. **Team** is the people who work with you. Each has a response SLA, a preferred channel and the approvals they hold. **Contacts** is everyone outside the team: clients, contractors, advisors, or anyone else you deal with. Contacts are private to you.

**What it does:**

- Add team members with their role, email, and their Slack, Discord and Telegram, picked by name.
- Set a response SLA so the Executive knows when a reply is overdue.
- Assign **authority scopes** (e.g. approve spend under $10K, sign off on hiring) so proposals route to the right person.
- Mark the principal (you) and set availability windows or on-leave dates.
- Track **open loops**: what each person owes. You can assign someone a task with a due date, and overdue ones are followed up automatically.
- Show how each team member answers the Executive's messages, and the writing rules it has learned for them.
- Keep **contacts** so the Executive can email or invite them, only when you ask it to directly (in the web app, or from your own Slack or Discord). A contact can't sign in, can't message the Executive, never approves anything, and is never chased.
- Keep contacts **private**: only you see them. Nobody else on your team sees the Contacts tab, finds a contact when they ask the Executive, or sees an alert about one.

**Team member or contact?**

| | Team member | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| Signs in to Open Executive (with an email) | Yes | No |
| Messages the Executive on Slack / Discord / Telegram | Yes | No |
| Approves proposals, gets check-ins and reminders | Yes | No |
| The Executive emails or invites them | On any task | Only when you ask directly |
| Who sees them | Everyone on the team | Only you |

**How to use:**

1. Open **Company** in the sidebar (it opens on **People**). Pick the **Team** or **Contacts** tab and click **Add person** (or **Add contact**). Only you, the principal, see the Contacts tab. Each card shows the person's name, role, preferred channel and one status, such as on leave.
2. Choose **Team member** or **Contact** at the top of the panel. Enter **Full name** (the only required field), **Role** (for a contact, **Role and company**, e.g. *Head of Procurement, Acme*) and **Email**. If this is you, tick **This is me — Primary**. You can only set this when adding someone, and the principal is always on the team.
3. For a team member, expand **Contact & routing**: **Preferred channel** (**Where they last talked**, Slack, Discord, Telegram or Email; with **Where they last talked** the Executive messages them in the chat app they last used with it, then any other app they have, then email), **Expected reply within *N* hours** (their SLA, default 24; items show as overdue on Home after that), and their **Slack**, **Discord** and **Telegram**. Those are also what lets this person talk to the Executive on those channels. For a contact, they are under **Chat apps**.
   - Pick each one by name: type to search, then click the person. With an email typed, Slack shows **Found by email** with their name already picked; click **Not them?** to choose someone else.
   - **Discord** lists the members of the bot's servers. If it can't (the bot's Server Members intent is off in Discord's developer settings), enter their ID by hand.
   - **Telegram** lists people who have messaged the bot. Not listed? Ask them to send the bot any message.
   - **Enter an ID by hand** under each one takes a raw ID instead. A chat app with no bot set up shows only the ID field.
4. For a team member, expand **Approval authority** and click each scope they hold:

   | Button | They receive |
   |---|---|
   | Spend <$2K / <$10K / >$10K | Proposals for spend in that range |
   | Hiring | Proposals related to hiring decisions |
   | Vendors | Proposals for vendor contracts |
   | Credit | Proposals involving credit or debt |
   | Legal | Proposals with legal implications |
   | Board | Proposals before board communications |
   | Meetings | Meetings the Executive wants to book |
   | All (wildcard) | Anything no one else is scoped for. Usually the principal |

5. Click **Add person** (or **Add contact**).

*A person's page*

Click a card to open the person. The page has up to four tabs:

- **Overview**: email, other addresses, how to reach them, and any leave date. Team members also show **Open loops** here.
- **Approvals & availability**: what they approve, and their **Availability windows** (days, start and end time, timezone). With no windows, they count as always available.
- **How they respond**: proactive messages sent to them over the last 30 days, and how many they answered. Kinds of message they reliably ignore are sent less often.
- **How I work with them**: how replies are written for them, learned from their own 👍/👎 and what they ask for in chats. Click **Edit rules** to type up to 8 rules, one per line; typed rules are always kept. The **⋯** menu has **Lock (stop learning)** / **Unlock (keep learning)** and **Reset what was learned**.

A contact's page has only **Overview**. An archived person has no **How they respond** or **How I work with them** tab.

*Change someone*

1. Click **Edit** at the top of their page. On **Overview** you can change the name, role, **Team member or contact**, email, **Other addresses** (one per line: mail from these reaches them and they can be emailed there; only the main email signs in), preferred channel and SLA. Slack, Discord and Telegram are under **Chat apps**, picked by name as when adding someone (it opens on its own when Slack finds them by email). **On leave until** is under **Advanced**.
2. To change approvals or availability, switch to **Approvals & availability** while editing: click scopes on or off, and use **Add window** / **Remove window**.
3. Click **Save**.
4. **Archive person**, in the **⋯** menu next to **Edit**, takes them off routing and the active roster. They get no new assignments; their history is kept. The principal can't be archived.

*Open loops*

- **Open loops** lists things a person committed to, was asked for in conversation, or was assigned. Overdue ones are followed up automatically. Click **Mark done** to close one.
- To assign a task, type it in **Assign a task** (up to 200 characters), optionally pick a **Due** date, and click **Assign**. The person is told once on their own channel, and the page says whether it reached them.

**Who can see and change it:**

- Only the principal can add, edit or archive people. Until someone is the principal, whoever sets up first can.
- Everyone signed in sees the team. Contacts stay yours alone.
- Anyone on the team can assign a task to anyone on the team. Only the principal and the person themselves see that person's open loops, **How they respond** and **How I work with them**, and only they can close a loop or change the working-style rules.

**Contacts I keep up to date:** with Act as me on and your own mailbox connected, the Executive adds people you emailed twice lately or met, and fills in a fuller name or a role from their own emails. Another address for someone you have is always asked first. It never changes what you typed. The **Contacts** tab shows **Changes I made**, each with **Undo**; **Got it** clears the list. A contact added this way shows **New** on its card, and its page says **Added by me on** the date, with **Undo** next to each change. Undo, or **Not now** on a suggestion, means it won't be proposed again. Switch **Keep my contacts up to date** to **On**, **Ask me first** (it lists **People to add**, each with **Add** or **Not now**) or **Off**. It skips your own company's addresses, mailing lists and no-reply mail. Only you see any of it.

**Phone, website and more:** the same pass copies a person's other contact details from their email signature: phone, mobile, website, LinkedIn, another profile and address. It keeps only what the email actually shows, and a website only on their own company's domain. It never changes or adds to what you typed (if you typed a phone, it leaves phone alone), and each one it adds is listed with **Undo**. You can type them too, under **Phone, website and more** when you edit someone, one per line like `Mobile: 555 010 0100`. Team members get these too.

**What I remember about a person:** the same pass keeps a short note on what you work on with each contact and team member, a few topics they're good to ask about, and when you last emailed, heard from and met them, plus your next meeting. The note comes only from emails you wrote them and meetings you set up. It shows as **What I remember** on their page, and the Executive uses it in chat to suggest who to ask. Only you see it, and removing the contact deletes it.

**Someone new wrote in:** when someone who isn't on People messages the Executive, their messages are held and a card **Who is *name*?** appears on Home. Click **Add them** and choose **Add as a new person** (enter their name and pick team or contact) or **Someone already on the list**. Their waiting messages are answered once they're added. **Ignore** is in the card's **⋯** menu. Only the principal sees these cards.

**Example from chat:** *"Add Sarah Chen as our fractional CFO — sarah@acme.com — she approves spend under $10k and usually replies within 48 hours."* Or: *"Add Jordan Lee from Acme as a contact — jordan@acme.example — and send them the proposal."* Or open **Add person**, press **Ctrl/Cmd + .**, and describe the person. The help panel (the sparkle button at the top right) fills in the panel for you to check and save.

**Forward it to the Executive:** forward an email from a client to the Executive's address and it replies to you, not them, with a summary, a draft reply you can send, any dates or commitments, and an offer to add the sender as a contact. Mail a contact sends the Executive directly is summarised for you, never answered on its own. Either way it stays between you and the Executive: it tells no one else, and any alert it raises is yours alone.

**Just for yourself?** When you use Open Executive just for yourself, setup adds only you, marked as the principal, with authority over everything. **People** sits in the sidebar under **You** and opens on **Contacts**. Anyone you add from chat is a contact unless you say otherwise, and the **Team** tab shows just you. Other team members are hidden in this mode; the page says how many. If you add a team member (or move a contact onto the team), Open Executive asks **Switch to team mode?**: click **Switch to team mode** or **Keep it just for me**. Home doesn't show a People tile in this mode.

*Note: authority scopes are how the Executive figures out who on the team to ask for any given approval.*
